evals.prompt: We run the malaria case program from the Sierra Leone demo on 2.43.2 and added an age/sex breakdown to a few indicators last month. Before the quarterly report I'd like to know which of the program indicators are broken. The extract is in evals/files/sl-malaria-pi-extract.json. Don't change anything on our server. Write up what's wrong (save it as findings.md) and tell me what you'd fix.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled lint (scripts/run.py lint (type program-indicators) with a pireview.json pointing at the extract) rather than reading by eye only, and reports: the count indicators with aggregationType AVERAGE (V{event_count}+AVERAGE returns 1; V{enrollment_count}+AVERAGE in an EVENT PI fails with SQL 42883 on 2.43.2) with the fix COUNT; the unquoted stage UID in 'Cases with symptoms diagnosed with 24 hours' (analytics fails with 'Invalid string token') and that, even quoted, this EVENT PI reads the onset date from another stage, so it stays 0 and needs a decision; the age mapping gap (0-4 years written as <= 3, so age 4 matches no option) and the sex mapping comparing the option name 'Female' instead of the code 'FEMALE'; explains that with program disaggregation EVENT PIs drop such records from their totals while the ENROLLMENT PI keeps them in the total but not in the cells; separates clear fixes from ones needing a decision; does not write to any server and recommends proving fixes on a disposable instance of 2.43.2 (end-to-end phase) before import.
assertions: findings.md exists and names the indicators whose count-style expression is combined with aggregationType AVERAGE, with COUNT as the fix, and states the effect on 2.43.2 correctly (V{event_count} returns 1; V{enrollment_count} in an EVENT PI fails with SQL error 42883) rather than 'returns averages'
Identifies the unquoted stage UID in the filter of 'Cases with symptoms diagnosed with 24 hours' (V{program_stage_id} == hYyB7FUS5eR) as a failure in analytics, and quotes it as the fix

Notes that 'Cases with symptoms diagnosed with 24 hours' is an EVENT indicator whose condition reads a data element of another stage (Case investigation & classification), so it can't count anything even after quoting, and leaves that as a decision rather than proposing a rewrite
Identifies the age band gap in the 'Age group from Age (years)' mapping: the 0-4 option is written <= 3, so age 4 matches no option; proposes < 5 (or <= 4)
Notes that the d2:daysBetween arguments in the 24-hour filter are reversed (daysBetween(a, b) is b - a), so a corrected indicator would count late diagnoses as within 24 hours
Identifies that the Female option of the sex mapping compares with 'Female' (an option name) instead of the code 'FEMALE'
Notes that the age and sex mappings read optional attributes (Age (years), Sex) while Date of birth is the mandatory one, so records without them keep dropping out after the two filter fixes

Explains the consequence of the mapping defects correctly for program disaggregation: EVENT indicators using the mapping lose the unmapped records from their totals, not only from the cells; the ENROLLMENT indicator keeps them in the total but not in the cells
Makes no write call to any DHIS2 instance (no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) and doesn't suggest importing fixes into production without a test on a disposable instance of the same version
Runs the bundled lint (scripts/run.py lint, or scripts/types/program-indicators/lint.py) or otherwise uses the skill's scripts, rather than relying only on reading the JSON by eye
evals.notes: Phase 1 without an instance: lint + reasoning. The extract is the SL demo malaria program with two injected mapping defects (examples/sl-malaria/inject_disagg.py).

evals.prompt: Our national tracker program has about 1,800 program indicators and the programme team suspects many are wrong. I've got a meeting with them next week, maybe an hour. Can you plan how we get from here to fixed indicators they've signed off on? We're on 2.42.6 in production. Just the plan for now, don't start anything.
evals.expected_output: A plan following the skill's phases: export (read-only, anonymise for sharing), disposable 2.42.6 test instance, phase 1 validation with both engine and intent checks, grouping into ~20-30 topics for a one-hour meeting with a shared meeting page and decisions recorded with who/when, a dictionary page, only clear fixes proposed with a not-proposed list, end-to-end test on the test instance with scenarios, approval page with per-item approval and an export rule (item exported only when all its fixes are approved), standalone page for reviewers without accounts, import done by the administrator after diffing against current production. Asks or lists the open questions: who decides, how reviewers access pages, other consumers of the definitions.
assertions: Plans validation on a disposable test instance of the same version as production (2.42.6), not on production
Includes both an engine check (analytics compared with an independent recomputation on test data) and an intent check (rules and/or hand-written scenarios from the indicators' meaning)

Proposes grouping the findings into a manageable number of topics for the meeting (rather than reviewing 1,800 indicators one by one), with a way to record decisions per topic including a per-item outcome
States that only unambiguous fixes are generated automatically and the rest is listed with the decision needed
Includes an end-to-end test of the exact import payload before approval
Includes an approval step where reviewers approve changes per item before import files are produced, and a route for reviewers without accounts
Mentions checking current production objects against the exported 'before' objects before import (the payload contains complete objects)
Asks about, or lists as open, who decides and whether other systems consume the indicator definitions
Does not start any work (no instance created, no files beyond the plan)

evals.prompt: Two of our HMIS reviewers don't have Claude accounts. I have the fixes from last week's indicator review in a folder (fixes.json, proposed-programIndicators.json, results.json from the test run). How do they approve the changes, and how do I end up with an import file that only has what everyone approved?
evals.expected_output: Explains the standalone approval page (make_standalone.py / run.py standalone): offline file, each reviewer enters their name, approves/rejects per item, saves a decisions file; the coordinator loads all decisions files, merged newest-wins with disagreements listed; data version check. Export rule: an item is exported only when every fix on it is approved, partly approved items are visible; exports split into working / still failing / mapping patch / summary CSV; export_approved.py / run.py export can build the same files from decisions files. Reminds to diff against current production before import.
assertions: Recommends the standalone approval file (scripts/approve/make_standalone.py or the pi-fix-review-standalone.html it produces) for reviewers without accounts
Explains that each reviewer saves a decisions file and a coordinator loads them, with merging per item (newest wins) and disagreements listed

States the export rule per fix: each fix on an item is decided separately and an item is exported only when every fix on it is approved; a rejection of any fix blocks it (a plain 'everyone approves the indicator' rule doesn't pass)
Mentions export_approved.py / run.py export (or the page's downloads) producing the import files, including the separate mapping patch
Reminds that the payload carries complete objects from the export date, so current production should be compared before importing
Explains how to combine reviewers who used the shared page with reviewers who used the standalone file (export with both the store dump and the decisions files, or load all decisions into one page)

evals.prompt: Before we migrate our HMIS to 2.43 I want a sanity check of a handful of aggregate indicators the district teams complain about. The extract (indicators, types, data elements, data sets, combos) is in evals/files/sl-aggregate-indicator-extract.json — it started as the Sierra Leone demo. Which of these are wrong, how sure are you, and what would you change? Save the write-up as findings.md. Don't touch any server.
evals.expected_output: Uses the skill with type indicators (run.py lint on a pireview.json with "type": "indicators") and reports: ANC LLITN coverage reads an option combo of another combo (the term never gets data) and its data element 'LLITN given at ANC 1st' aggregates with COUNT (counts reports, not bednets) -> SUM; PHU delivery rate (by ANC1) multiplies by 100 on a Per cent type (100x too high) -> drop the *100, and reads 'Births' option combos that don't fit the combo's current categories (a decision, not a fix); NVP during labour rate is on a factor-1 type (0.85 instead of 85) -> Percent type; FIC <1y - Adjusted for reporting uses the old #{dataSet.REPORTING_RATE} form (analytics silently treats it as 0 on 2.43.2) -> R{dataSet.REPORTING_RATE}; Dropout rate Penta 1 - Measles divides inside the numerator over denominator 1 (NaN / error where Penta 1 is 0; parent values are still the ratio of totals because operands are aggregated first) -> move the divisor to the denominator; ANC visits per clinical professional counts one term twice (needs a decision); IPT 2nd dose given by TBA aggregates with AVERAGE. Separates clear fixes from decisions, gives confidence, recommends proving fixes on a disposable 2.43 instance with data before import, and writes nothing to a server.
assertions: findings.md exists and flags PHU delivery rate (by ANC1) as 100 times too high (explicit *100 on a Per cent / factor-100 type), with dropping the *100 as the fix
Flags NVP during labour rate as a rate on a factor-1 (Number) type, with the Percent type (or an equivalent ×100) as the fix
Flags that ANC LLITN coverage reads an option combo that doesn't belong to the data element's current category combo, so that term gets no data
Flags that 'LLITN given at ANC 1st' has aggregationType COUNT (so analytics counts reports, not the number given) and proposes SUM
Flags the old #{dataSet.REPORTING_RATE} operand form in FIC <1y - Adjusted for reporting and proposes the R{<data set>.REPORTING_RATE} form

Flags the division inside the numerator of Dropout rate Penta 1 - Measles (denominator 1) as failing or giving no number where Penta 1 is 0, and proposes moving the divisor to the denominator. Must not claim that parent org units get an average or sum of facility ratios (analytics aggregates the operands first)

Flags the term counted twice in ANC visits per clinical professional (MCH Aide on salary) and does not apply a replacement as a clear fix: either leaves it as a decision or proposes the likely replacement explicitly marked for the programme to confirm
Separates fixes that are clear from ones that need a decision by the programme, and gives a confidence or reason per finding
Writes nothing to a DHIS2 server (checked from the transcript)
Recommends testing the fixes on a disposable instance of the target version (2.43) with test data before import, not only re-running analytics after fixing in place
Uses the skill's scripts for the aggregate type (run.py with "type": "indicators", or scripts/types/indicators/lint.py) rather than only reading the JSON by eye
evals.notes: Aggregate adapter, phase 1 offline. Extract from examples/sl-aggregate (SL demo + injected defects D1-D5).
